advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _pinned_environment_keys honor revoked_at_log_position (drop revoked keys) or route the pinned-basis verification through the era-aware verify_opcert path so a revoked pinned key cannot certify locally.
evidence: src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:474-478 returns `rec["public_key"]` filtered only on non-empty string, ignoring `revoked_at_log_position`
src/rebar/attest/trusted_env.py:137-143 keyring records carry `revoked_at_log_position`
src/rebar/attest/trusted_env.py:181-192 the merge path delegates the full keyring to `opcert.verify_opcert(... storage_anchor_commit=..., storage_anchor_position=...)` for era validity
src/rebar/attest/opcert.py:14 'Each key record carries explicit added_at_log_position/revoked_at_log_position' era boundaries
src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:660 `authorship.allowed_signers_from_keys(keys, principal)` binds keys with no era/revocation gating
advisory.finding: _pinned_environment_keys discards each pinned key's revoked_at_log_position / added_at_log_position and returns only public_key, so the local 'pinned_environment' trust basis certifies against a REVOKED pinned key. The merge-gate path (verify_required_environment -> opcert.verify_opcert) passes the full keyring and enforces era validity/revocation; the new local path does not, weakening the pinned trust root and applying even when verify.require_environment enforcement is ON.
scenarios: An operator pins a key for env A, later revokes it (revoked_at_log_position set) but leaves the record; a cert signed under the revoked key still reads 'certified' with trust_basis pinned_environment on a claim/close run
verify.require_environment set to A with A's key revoked: local path still accepts the revoked key while the merge gate would reject it

evidence: src/rebar/types.py:326-328 adds `# Which key certified an op-cert (bug c21f): ...` comment plus `trust_basis: NotRequired[str | None]`
src/rebar/types.py:1-13 banner: 'GENERATED. DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Regenerate with:: python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types'

docs/generated-artifacts.md:17 declares `src/rebar/types.py` derived from `src/rebar/schemas/*.schema.json`, regenerate with `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types`, enforced by the Public-types drift gate
src/rebar/schemas/gen_types.py:200-205 `_object_block` emits fields as bare `    {key}: {pytype}` with no inline comments, iterating `properties` in order
src/rebar/schemas/gen_types.py:138-140 `_pytype` maps an `enum` node to `Literal[...]`
src/rebar/schemas/verify_signature_result.schema.json:20-21 defines `trust_basis` with `enum:[own_key,pinned_environment,envelope_key,null]` and orders it BEFORE `rebar_version`
src/rebar/schemas/gen_types.py:349-356 `--check` compares generated text to the committed file byte-for-byte (`if current != text: return 1`)
tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py:48 pins `src/rebar/types.py` to `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types`
advisory.finding: src/rebar/types.py is a declared GENERATED artifact but was edited by hand in a way the generator does not produce, so the committed file no longer matches its source. The added inline comment is never emitted by the generator, the type is `NotRequired[str | None]` where the generator would emit a `Literal[...]` from the schema enum, and the field is placed after `rebar_version` where the generator emits `properties` order (trust_basis before rebar_version).
scenarios: Public-types drift gate runs `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types --check` and fails because the committed types.py differs from regenerated output (comment present, type is str|None not Literal, field ordering differs)
advisory.suggested_fix: Run `python -m rebar.schemas.gen_types` to regenerate src/rebar/types.py from verify_signature_result.schema.json; commit the generator's output (no inline comment, `trust_basis` as a `Literal[...]` placed before `rebar_version`).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that a cert signed by THIS environment reports `trust_basis == "own_key"` (not a disjunction).
evidence: src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:496-499: `if principal == own_principal: own_pubs = _opcert_own_public_keys(tracker); if own_pubs: return own_pubs, "own_key"`
tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_signature.py:143: `assert out["trust_basis"] in ("own_key", "envelope_key")`

ABSENCE: search for `own_key` across tests finds only the disjunction assertion at test_signature.py:143; no test asserts `trust_basis == "own_key"` for a same-environment-signed cert. Named input: `test_library_sign_then_certify` signs and verifies in the same environment and would exercise the own_key basis, but asserts only verdict, not trust_basis.
advisory.finding: The `own_key` trust_basis (same-environment signing) is never distinctly asserted. The added `_opcert_trust_root` returns `own_key` when `principal == own_principal`, but the only assertion touching it (tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_signature.py:143) is `assert out["trust_basis"] in ("own_key", "envelope_key")` — a disjunction that passes even if the same-environment path silently returned `envelope_key` instead of `own_key`. No test pins that a cert signed by THIS environment reports `trust_basis == "own_key"`.
scenarios: A regression that makes the own-key path fall through to envelope_key (e.g. `_opcert_own_public_keys` returning empty) would still leave line 143 green.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that writes a malformed `rebar.toml` and asserts a cross-environment cert still returns `certified` (fail-open on unreadable config).
evidence: src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:458-461: `try: return config.compose_config(root=repo_root).verify.require_environment or None ... except Exception: return None`
src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:456-457 docstring: `Fails OPEN on an unreadable config: an absent/broken rebar.toml must not silently turn a restriction ON that the operator never configured.`

ABSENCE: the only rebar.toml written in tests/unit/test_opcert_cross_environment_c21f.py is valid TOML via `_enforce` (line 128). Named violating input: a rebar.toml containing malformed TOML (e.g. `[verify\nrequire_environment = `) present while a cert from ENV_A is verified in ENV_B — the contract says it must still yield `certified`, not `foreign_key`.
advisory.finding: The `_required_environment` fail-open on an unreadable/malformed config — a security-relevant contract added in this diff ('an absent/broken rebar.toml must not silently turn a restriction ON') — is untested. No test writes a malformed rebar.toml and asserts a cross-environment cert still certifies (i.e. the broken config did NOT enable enforcement).
scenarios: A broken rebar.toml on disk; a regression narrowing the `except` clause would flip the behavior to fail-closed (enforcement on), blocking routine use, undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test writing invalid TOML to `store/rebar.toml`, then assert `signing.verify_signature(...)["verdict"] == "certified"` for an ENV_A-signed cert verified as ENV_B.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add unit tests for `embedded_public_key` covering: non-SSHSIG-magic blob, truncated wire string, and control-char keytype — each expecting `None`.
evidence: src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py:220-221: `if not blob.startswith(_SSHSIG_MAGIC): return None`
src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py:222-225: `pubkey_blob, _ = _read_sshsig_string(...)` guarded by `except ValueError: return None`
src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py:230-231: `if not keytype_str or _has_control_chars(keytype_str): return None`

ABSENCE: `search_files` for `embedded_public_key` under tests returns (no matches); only indirect coverage via `not-an-sshsig-blob` at test_opcert_cross_environment_c21f.py:308. Named violating inputs: a base64 blob NOT starting with `SSHSIG` (magic mismatch), a blob with `MAGIC` but a truncated pubkey length field (ValueError path), and a blob whose keytype string contains a control char.
advisory.finding: The newly-added `embedded_public_key` parser in sshsig.py has several defensive branches reachable only through added lines that are untested. Only the fully-unparseable input (`b"not-an-sshsig-blob"`) is exercised (returns None → foreign_key). The non-SSHSIG-magic-but-valid-base64 branch, the truncated wire-string branch (`_read_sshsig_string` raising ValueError), and the control-char keytype rejection have no test.
scenarios: A crafted or corrupted envelope reaching the envelope_key fallback; a regression in the length arithmetic of `_read_sshsig_string` would go uncaught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a small unit test calling `sshsig.embedded_public_key(...)` with (a) `base64`-armored non-magic bytes, (b) a `SSHSIG`-prefixed but truncated blob, (c) a blob whose keytype contains a control character, asserting each returns None.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_required_environment` fail CLOSED (or distinguish 'config absent' from 'config present-but-unreadable') so a broken `rebar.toml` cannot silently disable a set `verify.require_environment` restriction.
evidence: `_opcert_signing.py:458-461`: `try: return config.compose_config(root=repo_root).verify.require_environment or None` / `except Exception: ... return None`

`_opcert_signing.py:503-509`: `if required_env is not None: return [], None` — the `envelope_key` fallback (embedded public key from the blob under verification) is withheld ONLY when `required_env is not None`; a `None` result re-enables it.
`_opcert_signing.py:632-642`: the enforcement refusal (`principal != required_env -> foreign_key`) is entirely skipped when `_required_environment` returns `None`.

config.py:514 (compose_config docstring): 'A :class:`ConfigError` propagates (fail-closed startup), exactly as a direct load_config would.' — the rest of the config system is fail-CLOSED on a broken config; `_required_environment` alone catches and downgrades it to the permissive state.

Reachability: on a deployment that has SET `verify.require_environment` (the security-hardening posture), any exception path in `compose_config` (malformed TOML, I/O error, partial write) causes the restriction to evaporate and unpinned `envelope_key` certs (self-signed by any attacker who can write the attacker-writable tickets branch) to certify.
advisory.finding: `_required_environment` fails open: it swallows every exception from `compose_config` and returns `None`, which on the opt-in enforcement path silently disables the `verify.require_environment` trusted-set restriction and re-enables the `envelope_key` fallback. A deployment that opted into enforcement loses it whenever `rebar.toml` is broken or transiently unreadable.
scenarios: An operator enables `verify.require_environment`; a concurrent/partial write or a syntax error in `rebar.toml` makes it transiently unparseable — the enforcement restriction silently turns off and cross-environment `envelope_key` certs are accepted again.
An attacker who can perturb `rebar.toml` (corrupt/truncate) on an enforcing deployment drops the trusted-set restriction without leaving an obvious 'enforcement was on' signal at the verify call.
